ApiVersion.description: The major.minor version of the subordinate:plugin interface the plugin was built against, e.g. "0.1".

Capabilities.description:
`[capabilities]`: everything the sandbox opens only on request.

The manifest only *declares* these. Granting them is the install-time
approval step and enforcement is the host's, both in the crate's
`capability` module: an approval store records what the user approved, and
resolving it expands the roots into the sandbox's WASI preopens. Absent
keys mean "not requested", which is why parsing rejects unknown ones.

fs_read.description:
Roots the plugin may read, as `$PROJECT`-style roots or paths under
them.

network.description: Whether the plugin may open network connections.

shaders.description: Whether the plugin may have its WGSL shaders compiled and run.

dev.description: Whether it is a dev install: linked to its sources and watched.

location.description: Which of the two directories it went into.

mode.description:
How its files point at the source tree. A plain install is a
[`LinkMode::Copy`] snapshot that is never refreshed.

DevSource.description:
Where a dev install's files came from.

`root` is the directory holding `plugin.toml`; `wasm` is the built
component, which normally sits in a build directory well outside it.

changed.description:
False when it was already in that state, so a caller can tell a change
from a no-op.

enabled.description: Whether it is switched on now.

InstallLocation.description:
Where a plugin is installed.

The order is the precedence order: [`InstallLocation::Project`] is greater
than [`InstallLocation::User`] and wins an id conflict.

oneOf.description: The per-user plugin directory, shared by every project.

dev.description:
Link the install to its sources and watch them, instead of copying
once.

location.description: Which plugin directory to install into. Defaults to the per-user one.

path.description: The built `.wasm`, or the directory holding `plugin.toml`.

dev.description:
Whether it is a dev install: linked to a source tree, watched, and
reloaded when that tree is rebuilt (see [`crate::dev`]).

enabled.description: Whether it is switched on. Everything is on until switched off.

id.description: The identity from the manifest, which is the key everything uses.

location.description: Which of the two directories it was found in.

manifest.description:
Its whole parsed manifest, so a listing can show what it asks for
without reading the file again.

LinkMode.description: How a dev install's files point at the source tree.

oneOf.description: Each file is a symlink, so a rebuild is visible with no further work.

Each file is a copy, because this platform refused the symlink. The
copies are refreshed before every reload.

LoadFailure.description:
A plugin directory that could not be loaded.

Reported per plugin: the scan that produced it loaded every other plugin.
The three error fields are a [`SubError`] flattened, so the row carries a
stable code into JSON without the schema depending on the error type.

details.description: The error's details, e.g. the offending manifest field.

location.description: Which of the two directories it was found in.

capabilities.description: What the plugin asks to be allowed to do. Empty when absent.

mcp.description: The MCP tools the plugin contributes. Empty when absent.

plugin.description: Identity, interface version and the worlds implemented.

McpSection.description: `[mcp]`: the MCP tools the plugin contributes.

tools.description: Tools by name, as they appear to an agent.

description.description: What the tool does, used verbatim as the MCP tool description.

schema.description: The tool's input JSON Schema, relative to the plugin directory.

PluginSection.description: `[plugin]`: who the plugin is and what it implements.

api.description: The `subordinate:plugin` interface version it was built against.

description.description: One-sentence description, shown in the plugins panel.

PublishedTool.description:
One tool as `plugin.tools` publishes it over the Command API.

The MCP bridge turns a row of this straight into a tool: `name` is the tool
name a client calls, `input_schema` its argument schema, and `plugin` and
`tool` are what the bridge sends back when the tool is called.

input_schema.description: The argument schema from the manifest.

name.description:
The MCP tool name: the plugin id with dots turned into underscores, an
underscore, then the plugin-local name.

plugin.description: The plugin that contributes the tool.

title.description: The dotted, human-facing name: plugin id, a dot, the local name.

tool.description: The plugin-local name, as the component's `call` takes it.

ReloadError.description: One error, flattened the way [`crate::registry::LoadFailure`] flattens one.

ReloadStatus.description:
What the last load of one plugin did.

This is the row a plugins panel shows (TASK-98) and what `plugin.reload`
answers. A failed reload keeps the counts of the version that is still
loaded, because that is the version still answering.

commands.description: How many menu commands the loaded version registers.

dev.description: Whether it is a dev install.

error.description:
Why the last attempt failed, when it did. The counts above then still
describe the previous version, which stayed loaded.

generation.description:
How many times it has loaded successfully in this process. A dev
install's reloads are how a developer knows the rebuild landed.

tools.description: How many MCP tools it contributes.

Scan.description: Everything one walk of the plugin directories found.

failures.description: The directories that did not, sorted by path.

plugins.description: The plugins that loaded, sorted by id.

shadowed.description: The copies that lost an id conflict, sorted by path.

Shadowed.description:
A plugin that is installed but not loaded, because another copy of the same
id won.

directory.description: The directory of the copy that is *not* used.

shadowed_by.description: The directory of the copy that won.

plugins.description: One row per plugin that has been loaded in this process, in id order.

ToolFailure.description:
One plugin whose declared tools could not be published.

Reported per plugin, like a [`LoadFailure`]: a plugin with an unreadable or
uncompilable tool schema hides its own tools and nobody else's.

details.description: The error's details, e.g. the offending tool.

id.description: The plugin whose tools are missing from the listing.

ToolListing.description:
The result of `plugin.tools`: every MCP tool the enabled plugins contribute.

The MCP bridge asks for this when a client lists tools, and publishes each
row beside its own tools under the plugin-id prefix the row carries
(docs/PLAN.md §6.2, §7). Nothing here is loaded from a component: the
manifest is what the user approved on install, so a tool is listed as the
manifest declares it whether or not the plugin is instantiated yet.

failures.description: The plugins whose tools could not be published, sorted by id.

tools.description: The tools, sorted by published name.

World.description: A WIT world a plugin can implement (docs/PLAN.md §6.2).

oneOf.description: Parameters plus WGSL shaders, with an optional CPU fallback.
Block-based f32 audio processing under a real-time budget.
Turns a file or URL into media items or a sequence.
Encoder presets or a whole custom export target.
New editing commands built from Command API primitives.
Extra MCP tools the core forwards calls to.
